source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin campus publishes 19 MW of IT capacity across 242,000 square feet, and that is the only power figure the operator discloses.

The disclosure stops there. The spec page does not divide the 19 MW between the two buildings, does not state a power density per rack, and does not name a tenant. Any rack count derived from 19 MW depends entirely on an assumed density, so the data supports no rack figure at all. The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, describe what the campus is permitted to host, not who occupies it.

For AI specifically, the useful fact is the gap between a published capacity number and the information needed to reason about compute. A training cluster's footprint depends on power per rack and total load together, and only one of those is public here. The 19 MW is real as a disclosure, but it cannot be converted into accelerators, racks, or jobs without assumptions the operator has not supplied.

In Texas this campus ranks tenth among the 19 facilities in the state with a published megawatt figure, against a published state total of 475.41 MW, about 4 percent. Texas has 137 mapped facilities, and most publish no figure, so the 19 with numbers are a self-selected slice. That share measures disclosure, not the grid, and the grid is not described in this data.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
